5. Turbine foundation: concrete and reinforcement
The foundation is a circular gravity base on a prepared formation. The main body shall be cast in one
continuous pour. Before the main pour the Contractor shall place 58 m3 of C20/25 blinding concrete across
the formation, finished to within 10 mm of level.
The main slab requires 620 m3 of C30/37 concrete, exposure class XC4 XF1 XA1. The pedestal above it is a
higher class: allow 70 m3 of C50/60 concrete for the pedestal, placed no later than 14 days after the slab.
Reinforcement shall be B500B to the bending schedules. The total reinforcing steel for the foundation is 78 t,
delivered in cut and bent bundles and tagged by bar mark. Couplers are included in this figure. Spacers and
tying wire are by the Contractor and need not be listed.
5.1 Tower anchorage
The anchor cage is supplied by the Contractor in structural steel grade S355, with a total mass of 13.5 t
including the top and bottom flanges. Under the tower flange the Contractor shall place 3 m3 of high-strength
cementitious grout. Levelling pads shall use 400 kg of epoxy levelling mortar.
5.2 Protection of buried surfaces
All buried concrete faces shall receive two coats of bitumen coating. Allow 600 kg of bitumen coating for the
foundation. Do not apply in rain or below 5 degrees C.

6. Earthworks and drainage
Excavated material that does not meet the backfill specification goes off Site. Material brought in shall be
tested at source. The quantities in Table 6-1 are for the foundation and crane pad together.
Item Material Quantity Unit
6.1 Crushed stone backfill 0/45 1150 t
6.2 Gravel drainage layer 2/32 170 t
6.3 Geotextile separation layer 500 g/m2 1300 m2
6.4 HDPE drainage pipe DN110 240 m
Table 6-1: earthworks and drainage materials.
HDPE drainage pipe weighs 1.1 kg/m. Falls shall be at least 1 in 100 towards the outfall. Temporary
formwork for the foundation and the substation slab is expected to need about 8 t of timber formwork, to be
taken back by the supplier where possible.

7. Cabling
Cables run from the turbine transformer position to the collector substation in a single trench. Electrical
design is by others; the Contractor supplies and installs to the cable schedule below.
Cable or duct Length (m) Mass (kg/m)
MV cable 3 x 1 x 240 mm2 aluminium conductor 1750 1.95
LV cable 4 x 95 mm2 copper conductor 300 3.4
Copper earthing tape 25 x 3 mm 220 0.67
PVC cable duct DN160 850 2.6
Mass figures refer to conductor metal only for the cables and to the whole product for the tape and the duct.
Sheath, insulation and joint kits are excluded from the mass column.

pages.5:
8. Collector substation
The substation stands on a reinforced slab. The slab takes 80 m3 of C25/30 concrete and 9 t of reinforcing
steel B500B. Support structures for the busbars and the transformer bund shall be galvanised steel, 17 t in
total, hot-dip galvanised after fabrication.
For site mortar and small repairs allow 5.5 t of cement CEM II/A 42.5. Busbars shall be aluminium busbar,
1.1 t in total, supplied with all clamps.
8.1 Equipment
Equipment Quantity Unit Remark
Power transformer 25 MVA 110/20 kV 36 t Shipping mass, drained
Transformer oil top-up 1 t Mineral oil, IEC 60296
MV switchgear panel 6 pcs Gas-insulated, SF6-free
Factory acceptance tests shall be witnessed by the Employer. The transformer oil quantity is in addition to
the oil filled at the factory.
